newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Oman LNG aims for financing, EPC deal in "weeks".
newsitem.headline: Oman LNG aims for financing, EPC deal in "weeks".

text.p: Oman LNG Company, downstream operator of Oman's liquefied gas export plan, expects to sign the project's main financing and construction contracts in weeks, Tony Hanna, Oman LNG general manager said on Monday.

"Within the next few weeks all agreements related to the Company will be signed and the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract awarded," Hanna told delegates at a gas conference in Abu Dhabi.
Oman LNG Co -- responsible for the liquefaction plant, transportaion and sales -- is 51 percent owned by the government and the rest of the equity is split with foreign firms.

Royal Dutch Shell Group unit Shell Overseas Trading Ltd owns 34 percent, Total SA six percent, Partex (Oman) Corp two percent, Mitsubishi Corp and Mitsui and Co Ltd three percent each and ITOCHU Corp one percent.
A commitment from seven international arranger banks for a $2.25 billion project loan was secured in June.

The final bank underwriting will clear the way to award the project's EPC contract and the official signing of a firm supply agreement with the Korea Gas Corp (KGC) for an annual 4.1 million tonnes of Omani gas from the year 2000.

Japan's Chiyoda and Foster Wheeler Corp were selected last May to carry out the $1.2 billion contract to build a liquefaction plant at al-Ghalilah capable of producing an anuual 6.6 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas.
KGC and Oman LNG Co concluded a long-term sales and purchase agreement for the 4.1 million tonnes in August.
"The Gas Supply Agreement with the (Oman) government has been finalised as well as all other service agreements that the project requires," Hanna said.
The seven banks arranging the loans are ABN-Ambro, National Westminister Bank Plc, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Citibank, Banque Indosuez, Korea Exchange Bank and Gulf International Bank.
